_read_me: This is the durable, checkable validation-state record referenced by docs/release-validation-plan.md's 'Validation State Tracking' section. Read that section before editing this file by hand. Never hand-wave an entry as validated: every non-null commit/date/validator/evidence_ref below must correspond to a real, completed validation run with real evidence (command output, CI run URL, or a PR/issue comment quoting it) -- see the proposed AG-REL-011 rule's exact text in PR #1368's body (still open/Draft as of 2026-08-01, not yet merged into AGENTS.md). Corrected 2026-08-01: this note previously pointed at 'AG-VAL-028', a rule number this project's docs originally proposed for this exact purpose but which was never adopted under that number and was later independently reassigned to an unrelated rule (periodic CI-checkability review of manual-review-only rules); the live proposal covering a stale validation-state.json record specifically is AG-REL-011, not AG-VAL-028. This file is intentionally seeded with 'never validated' placeholders; it must not be pre-filled with a fabricated pass.
invalidation_notice_2026_07_25: FULL INVALIDATION per this file's own full_invalidation_triggers: AGENTS.md changed multiple times on 2026-07-25 (AG-CI-014; AG-CI-015 via PR #1242, a different rule than the one originally proposed under that number in the same-day CI-stabilization work, which is being renumbered to avoid the collision; AG-GH-008 correction; AG-WF-027) after this record's last_stack_validation/last_ci_validation commit (88ddbf6a). Per this file's own stated policy, a governance-doc change is a blanket invalidation trigger for EVERY subsystem in both layers, not a per-subsystem one -- every entry below must be treated as stale regardless of its own recorded commit/date until a fresh full pass (both Part A and Part B) actually runs and updates this file with real evidence. This note is added honestly rather than silently leaving the below looking current; no entry below has been re-verified as part of adding this note or the corresponding docs/release-validation-plan.md rows for 2026-07-25's changes (actionlint SIGKILL guard, BuildKit build-tools-image concurrency serialization, Q1 build-tools.yml trigger narrowing, the runner-host cleanup script, CVE-2026-34040's non-exploitability documentation, and the governance rule changes named above) -- those are new checklist entries only, not evidence of a completed run against them.
invalidation_notice_2026_08_01: STILL FULLY INVALID, gap now WIDER than the 2026-07-25 note above -- added honestly per AG-REL-011 (proposed, PR #1368): no fresh validation pass of any kind has run since last_stack_validation/last_ci_validation's recorded commit (88ddbf6a, 2026-07-24). As of this note, origin/current_dev's tip is 433c3fd2 -- 274 commits ahead of 88ddbf6a over 2026-07-24 through 2026-08-01. `bash scripts/untracked/classify-image-impact.sh 88ddbf6a 433c3fd2` reports every one of dns_rust/dns_image/ui/watchdog/dhcp/dhcp_proxy/ntp/proxy/build_tools/workflow/docs/governance/setup_runtime/deploy/release_contract/scripts as true (IMAGE_IMPACT=true) -- i.e. this is not a narrow, incremental gap scoped to one or two subsystems; essentially the entire classifier surface has changed. governance=true confirms AGENTS.md/.github/AGENTS.md changed again multiple times in this window (re-firing full_invalidation_triggers repeatedly, not just once more), independent of and on top of the 2026-07-25 trigger already recorded above -- deploy/dev/ was retired (#766), config/prod and deploy/quickstart/prod/full-setup compose files changed, services/watchdog gained a new retention.sh extraction + hardening (PR #1360, merged) alongside a still-open, unmerged parallel Rust-crate scaffold (PR #1355, see docs/release-validation-plan.md's Coverage Assessment), scripts/lib/validation-image-tag.sh and scripts/untracked/select-build-tools-image.sh got a real case-sensitivity security fix (issue #842/PR #1360), a real CI tag-commit race surfaced and was worked around but not structurally fixed (PR #1354), a known digest-mismatch limitation (issue #1348) was consolidated into the still-open #1095 CI-pipeline rework, and a build-push.yml self-modification trigger bug remains open and under live investigation (PR #1367 POC). None of last_stack_validation, last_ci_validation, or any subsystem_validation entry below has been re-run or re-verified as part of adding this note -- they remain exactly as recorded on 2026-07-24 and must be treated as stale evidence only, not current, for any release-readiness purpose (AG-REL-011). A fresh, full Part A + Part B validation pass against current_dev's actual tip is still outstanding and is a separate, larger piece of work not undertaken here.
invalidation_notice_2026_08_02: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED, then immediately re-triggered again -- recorded honestly rather than silently rounded to 'fixed'. A real, full Part B stack-validation pass ran against current_dev's tip at commit 885e2f40 (2026-08-02, for the actual v0.3.0 branch-promotion readiness check) and is now recorded below in last_stack_validation and the relevant subsystem_validation entries: 8 of 9 Part B scenarios PASS with real evidence (including finally closing the Admin UI cache-resize gap left open since 2026-07-24), 1 (watchdog) PARTIAL -- see last_stack_validation.summary for the honest per-scenario detail. Part A (CI) was deliberately NOT re-run as part of this pass -- that evidence instead comes from the promotion PR's own fresh CI run, not re-recorded here as a separate pass; last_ci_validation below remains the 2026-07-24/88ddbf6a record and is not claimed current. IMMEDIATELY AFTER this pass began, current_dev's tip advanced again to 7e5c0104 (PR #1390, adding AG-REL-013 to AGENTS.md) -- per this file's own full_invalidation_triggers, any AGENTS.md change is a blanket invalidation trigger, so strictly this record is already stale again for a literal reading of that rule. This specific instance is judged low-risk (AG-REL-013 is a process-documentation-only addition describing the branch-promotion procedure itself, with zero product-code/runtime-behavior change), so the maintainer decision recorded here is to treat the below as valid evidence for the v0.3.0 promotion covering commit 885e2f40 without re-running Part B again for 7e5c0104 specifically -- but this is a judgment call, not a mechanical pass, and is written down as such rather than silently absorbed. Two further gaps were found IN the validation plan/checklist itself during this pass (not in the product) and are tracked in issue #1391, not fixed here: a Bring-up shortcut that can silently produce a broken environment without a prior `setup.sh install`, and two documentation inaccuracies (a wrong port number, a missing/wrong CA path) in Part B's DNS section. `ntp` remains completely unvalidated (see its still-null entry below) -- also tracked in #1391, not addressed in this pass.

last_stack_validation.validator: claude-agent (dispatched Part B stack-validation pass, docs/release-validation-plan.md Part B, for the real v0.3.0 branch-promotion readiness check)
last_stack_validation.scope: All 9 Part B scenarios: bring-up, DNS resolution both modes, DHCP all three modes, cache HIT/MISS (HTTP + SSL/MITM HTTPS), NATS full secondary lifecycle, Admin UI reachability + dashboard + cache-resize, watchdog auto-restart coverage, central logging/syslog forwarding, resource-leak/cleanup pass. Ran against the real, already-published sha-885e2f4 first-party images (confirmed via each image's own org.opencontainers.image.revision label, no local rebuild needed) on self-hosted Linux runners (lancache-241 main stack, lancache-243 isolated DHCP simulations), after confirming no runner was mid-job.
last_stack_validation.summary: 8 of 9 scenarios PASS with real evidence. Bring-up PASS (all containers healthy). DNS PASS (dig + openssl s_client confirmed real passthrough CDN cert in standard mode, real LanCache-NG CA cert in SSL/MITM mode). DHCP PASS for all three modes via the canonical simulation scripts (Kea full DORA + TSIG DDNS + isolation negative control; dnsmasq-proxy PXE-tagged offers correct per architecture, non-PXE client correctly gets none; dnsmasq-relay lease correctly sourced from the client-subnet pool via giaddr, proving real routing). Cache HIT/MISS PASS for both HTTP and SSL/MITM HTTPS (byte-identical MISS-then-HIT, query-string invariance confirmed, standard-mode HTTPS confirmed genuinely uncached). NATS PASS (full secondary lifecycle via nats-secondary-auth-callout-simulation.sh: isolation, active-disconnect via real connz polling, rotation/removal credential invalidation, xkey encryption confirmed via packet capture). Admin UI PASS, INCLUDING closing the cache-resize gap left open since 2026-07-24 (PR #1174): POST /cache/resize -> converge-reconcile -> a real docker compose up -d proxy recreate this time -> nginx -T confirmed the new max_size, the headline criterion left unproven in the 2026-07-24 pass. Syslog PASS (real nginx access-log lines from the cache tests confirmed arriving at syslog-ng via fluent-bit). Resource-leak/cleanup PASS (docker ps -a / docker volume ls empty after down -v, stable FD count across NATS restarts). Watchdog auto-restart PARTIAL: nats fully proven per the plan's prescribed method (external docker kill --signal=STOP, genuine hang, new StartedAt). dns-standard was restart-tested but via docker stop (a crash), not the prescribed hang method -- red-transition and restart confirmed, but not the specific scenario asked for. proxy's SIGSTOP attempt found and verified a real gap in the TEST TECHNIQUE, not a confirmed product bug: docker kill --signal=STOP only ever signals the container's PID 1 (nginx master); for a multi-process container the 8 worker processes plus cache manager/loader stay S (sleeping) and keep serving requests throughout (confirmed via /proc/<pid>/status), so it remains genuinely unknown whether Watchdog would detect a real full nginx hang -- docker pause (cgroup freezer) is recommended instead for any monitored service that is not single-process. dns-ssl was not tested this pass (time budget). Two additional Part B documentation inaccuracies were found and are NOT fixed here (tracked in issue #1391): the DNS section names port :8443 for standard-mode HTTPS where :443 is what's externally reachable, and the plan never states the real CA path (deploy/<profile>/certs/ca.crt, not a repo-root certs/ca.crt). Also found and NOT fixed here (tracked in #1391): a plain `docker compose up` against deploy/quickstart with no prior `setup.sh install` actually fails (docker-socket-proxy and nats both fail to start, due to bind-mount sources setup.sh's own asset-install step would normally populate) -- worked around by hand during this pass rather than reflecting a supported operator path. `ntp` was out of scope for this pass (no Part B scenario exists for it yet -- see #1391) and remains fully unvalidated, see its own entry below.
last_stack_validation.evidence_ref: https://github.com/wiki-mod/lancache-ng/pull/1392 (this record's own introducing PR); https://github.com/wiki-mod/lancache-ng/issues/1391 (the checklist-level findings from this pass)

last_ci_validation.validator: claude-agent (Part A CI validation pass, real Linux self-hosted runner host)
last_ci_validation.summary: Real Part A (CI) pass against the frozen v0.3.0 branch tip (identical content to current_dev at this commit): cargo fmt/check(-D warnings)/clippy(-D warnings)/test PASS for all three crates (ui 353 tests, dns/nats-subscriber 49 tests, pxe-client-probe 4 tests) on real Linux via the same rustup-stable toolchain CI itself installs. dhcp-relay-flow-simulation.sh PASS (real two-segment DORA relay proof). nats-secondary-auth-callout-simulation.sh run twice against locally-built images pinned to this exact commit (ghcr.io nightly was stale/behind at run time): positive control PASS (connz-polled active-disconnect #681, xkv1 encryption marker #682 with no plaintext JWT marker), negative control (xkey removed) correctly FAILED with the expected plaintext-marker error. check-vex-drift.sh PASS + negative control (mutated .trivyignore.yaml) correctly failed with a real diff. setup_update_idempotence.bats guard PASS + negative control (NTP_ENABLED removed) correctly failed naming that key. shellcheck: 0 findings. bats tests/bats: 714/715 pass -- the 1 real failure (check-bats-path-filter-coverage.sh's own self-test) was root-caused to a genuine gap (dnsmasq-relay.conf.template missing from build-tools.yml's path filters) and fixed in PR #1209, re-verified there (0 gaps after fix). shellspec: 3/3 pass. actionlint (default invocation, matching CI's own exact 'Run ShellCheck and ActionLint' step): FAILED to complete -- hung indefinitely, reproduced 3/3 times at this commit; corroborated by a real, independently-stuck CI job (shellcheck job on PR feat/681-nats-active-disconnect, in_progress 5+ hours using the actual published ghcr.io build-tools image, not a local-build artifact). Disabling the embedded shellcheck integration (-shellcheck=) completes in 0.017s with 0 findings, so the workflow YAML content itself is clean; the check as CI currently invokes it is not reliably completing. UPDATE (maintainer follow-up, same day): after this hang was flagged, the maintainer audited the rest of the run queue and found 7 more runs stuck the identical way (in_progress for hours at the same step, several on already-merged/deleted branches), all cancelled -- confirming this is a systemic slot-leak, not a one-off, and that a meaningful share of what looked like general runner-pool congestion during this validation pass was actually these zombie runs never releasing their slots. See PR #1213's comments for the full list of affected runs. Not exercised in this pass (explicitly deferred, not silently assumed passing): DHCP-Kea and dnsmasq-ProxyDHCP live E2E simulations (dhcp-kea-lease-flow-simulation, dhcp-proxy-pxe-simulation), DNS live dig-based resolution and setup-reset-dns-config-simulation.sh, check-workflow-service-lists.sh, Admin UI/watchdog live Part B stack checks (out of Part A CI scope by design), governance-doc manual review beyond the plan-doc fix itself. NOT re-run as of the 2026-08-02 Part B pass above -- a fresh Part A record against current_dev's current tip is still outstanding (the promotion PR's own CI run provides fresh evidence for that specific PR, but is not re-recorded here as a standalone Part A pass).

setup-runtime.note_2026_08_05_update_health_baseline: NARROW ADDITION, not a full re-validation of this subsystem -- recorded honestly rather than rounded up. Issue #1391's post-merge-verification pass (2026-08-05) found a real, reproducible bug in `setup.sh update`'s post-update health gate: it failed on ANY currently-unhealthy non-UI service, so a pre-existing, unrelated failure (ntp crash-looping under this project's LXC CAP_SYS_TIME limitation, issue #1296) permanently blocked every future update. Fixed in a dedicated PR (branch fix/1391-update-health-baseline, Refs #1391) by adding capture_stack_health_baseline()/a baseline-aware wait_for_stack_health -- see docs/release-validation-plan.md Part B section 12 (renumbered from an earlier draft's section 10 once merged alongside this same issue's other new sections 10/11) for the full scenario writeup. Proven two ways on a self-hosted runner: (1) tests/bats/setup_update_health_baseline.bats, 9 deterministic cases, no real Docker needed; (2) a real, live, hands-on run -- fresh setup.sh install with ntp enabled, confirmed crash-looping for the same reason #1296 already root-caused, then a real setup.sh update completed instead of rolling back, reporting 'Proceeding despite service(s) unhealthy before this update started too: ntp'; a deliberately injected real regression (docker-compose.override.yml forcing nats's previously-passing healthcheck to always fail) then still correctly triggered rollback via rollback_stack_update/cmd_restore. This closes ONLY this one specific gap -- the rest of this subsystem entry's caveats (commit/date/validator/evidence_ref above, still pointing at the 2026-07-24/#1213 record) remain exactly as stale as already documented; this is not a full setup-runtime re-validation.

full_invalidation_triggers: AGENTS.md or .github/AGENTS.md changed since the recorded commit (governance change can redefine what 'correct' means for every subsystem, not just one)

The diff since the recorded commit could not be reconstructed (force-push discarding the old tip, an unreachable base, or any case classify-image-impact.sh itself would fall back to --all-changed for) -- treat as fully stale rather than guessing
The recorded commit is not an ancestor of the commit under test (a rebase/history-rewrite happened) -- re-derive the diff from a real merge-base, do not assume the old record still applies
